author: Daniel Watts
message: My inverter has been showing fault code E032 since yesterday evening. It is still running but I am worried.

author: Laura Chen
message: Thank you for reaching out. E032 indicates a grid overvoltage event. Can you tell me what firmware version your inverter is running? You can find this in the Settings menu.

author: Daniel Watts
message: It says firmware 3.5.1 on the display.

author: Laura Chen
message: Version 3.5.1 has a known sensitivity issue with grid voltage transients. I am dispatching a technician to check your grid connection point and will push the 3.5.2 patch remotely once the hardware check is complete.

author: Stormy Weathers
message: There was a big thunderstorm last night and now my battery will not charge at all. The app just shows a red exclamation mark.

author: Marcus Adler
message: I can see from the BMS logs that the overcurrent protection fired at 23:47. This is a safety measure to protect the battery from surge damage. I need to run a remote cell balance check before re-enabling charging. Please do not attempt to reset the unit manually.

author: Marcus Adler
message: Cell balance check complete. All cells within normal tolerance. I have cleared the overcurrent flag remotely. Your battery should now start accepting charge. Please monitor for the next 2 hours and let me know the SoC reading.

author: Stormy Weathers
message: Charging again! SoC is already at 34%. Thank you so much for the quick help.

author: Sunny Sunshine
message: My solar panels seem to be producing much less than usual. I used to get around 25 kWh on a sunny day like today but the app only shows 15 kWh so far.

author: Maria Kowalski
message: The monitoring dashboard has not updated since Tuesday. It is still showing data from 3 days ago.

author: Laura Chen
message: I can see the gateway is online but the API authentication is failing. This happens when the OAuth token expires. I am renewing it now on the backend.

author: Laura Chen
message: Token renewed. Dashboard should refresh within the next 5 minutes. The underlying data was being collected the whole time so you will see the backfilled readings shortly.

author: Maria Kowalski
message: Everything is back to normal now. Thank you for sorting it out so quickly!

author: Sophie Dupont
message: My inverter is running but it says export is blocked. I have a feed-in-tariff contract and this is losing me money every day.

author: Marcus Adler
message: I have checked with the grid operator and there is a temporary export curtailment order for your postcode due to local grid congestion. This is outside our control unfortunately. I have escalated to the regulatory liaison team to expedite the exemption request.

author: Hans Mueller
message: The inverter has been making a loud grinding noise for the past 2 days. It is coming from the fan area I think. The system is still producing power.

author: Laura Chen
message: Grinding from the cooling fan usually means bearing wear. As long as the unit is producing normally and no temperature alarms are showing, it is safe to continue operating. I have ordered a replacement fan assembly and will schedule an engineer visit.

author: Priya Sharma
message: I set up my EV charger to use excess solar but it never actually starts charging from solar. It just waits for me to start it manually.

author: Marcus Adler
message: I can see the charger is using OCPP 1.6 but your inverter's smart home interface expects SunSpec Modbus. They cannot talk to each other directly. I am researching a middleware bridge solution and will update you by end of week.

author: Emma Johnson
message: During our routine annual inspection, my installer found a hotspot on one panel. They said it could be serious. Should I be worried?

author: Laura Chen
message: Hotspots can indicate cell degradation or delamination and should be taken seriously. I have flagged this as high urgency and raised a warranty replacement order. Until the panel is replaced, please ask your installer to isolate that string if the hotspot temperature exceeds 80°C.

author: Kenji Tanaka
message: My inverter stopped working after it tried to update itself. It is just showing a blinking LED now and nothing on the display.

author: Marcus Adler
message: The inverter is in firmware recovery mode after an interrupted OTA update. This is recoverable. I am initiating a remote rescue firmware push now. Please keep the AC supply on and do not touch any buttons.

author: Marcus Adler
message: Recovery firmware successfully installed. The inverter has rebooted and is now running 3.7.2. Production has resumed. I recommend enabling automatic update scheduling during overnight hours to avoid future interruptions.

author: Kenji Tanaka
message: Everything is working perfectly again. Great support!

author: Thomas Bergmann
message: We had a short power cut last night and the battery did not power the house. Everything went dark. I thought the whole point was to have backup power.

author: Laura Chen
message: I can see from the logs that the battery backup mode was not enabled on your system. It defaults to off and must be explicitly configured. I will schedule a remote configuration call with you today to enable emergency backup and set your priority loads.

author: Maria Kowalski
message: My installer called me saying there is water inside the junction box. They are concerned about safety. What should we do?

author: Marcus Adler
message: Please isolate the DC array immediately by opening the array disconnect switch. Do not operate the system until the junction box is replaced. I am prioritizing a replacement part shipment and will keep you updated on the delivery ETA.

author: Carlos Rodriguez
message: My installer noticed corrosion on some connectors during a checkup. Are my panels in danger? Will it affect my warranty?

author: Laura Chen
message: Corroded MC4 connectors are a fire and arc fault risk and must be replaced promptly. Your system warranty covers manufacturing defects but installer workmanship is covered by the installation guarantee. I have opened a priority work order for connector replacement.

author: Daniel Watts
message: Our safety officer tested the rapid shutdown system during a fire safety drill and it did not activate. This is a serious safety concern. We need this fixed urgently.

author: Marcus Adler
message: This is a critical safety issue. I have escalated to our safety engineering team immediately. As a precaution, please do not allow anyone on or near the roof until this is resolved. I will have an engineering response within 2 hours.

author: Luca Ferretti
message: My AC isolator keeps tripping every few days. There is no obvious fault code but the system goes offline until I reset it manually.

author: Laura Chen
message: Random nuisance tripping without fault codes often points to the arc fault detection circuit being overly sensitive. I have remotely adjusted the arc detection threshold from level 3 to level 2 and enabled extended trip logging. Please let me know if it trips again.

author: Priya Sharma
message: The app is showing a ground fault warning on string 1 and the inverter has shut down that string. What does this mean and is it safe?

author: Marcus Adler
message: A ground fault means current is leaking to earth somewhere on the DC string. The inverter correctly isolated the string as a safety measure. Do not attempt to reset it manually. I have dispatched a qualified electrician with a ground fault locator. Please keep children away from the roof area.

author: Thomas Bergmann
message: I found chewed cables on my roof today. It looks like an animal got to the solar wiring. The system is showing arc fault errors.

author: Laura Chen
message: Pest damage to DC cables is a serious arc fault risk. Your inverter's arc protection has correctly shut down the affected string. Do not re-enable it. I am scheduling an emergency cable replacement and will also recommend installing protective cable conduit to prevent recurrence.

author: Stormy Weathers
message: My system exported to the grid all day even though we have a zero-export agreement with the utility. I got a warning letter from them today.

author: Marcus Adler
message: I can see from the logs that the zero-export relay failed to activate yesterday. A worn relay contact is the likely cause. I have flagged this as urgent and will have a replacement relay shipped for next-day installation. In the meantime I have set a conservative export limit via software curtailment as a temporary measure.

author: Luca Ferretti
message: The solar tracker on my ground mount installation stopped moving this morning. All the panels are pointed east and just staying there all day. I am losing a lot of production.

author: Laura Chen
message: The tracker controller is not responding to position commands. This looks like a controller board failure rather than a communication issue. I have ordered a replacement controller and it will be shipped express. Your system will produce at a reduced but safe fixed-tilt output until the repair is complete.
